description: Primary key. Also appears in orders.customer_id as a foreign key. When joining customers and orders, always qualify (e.g. c.customer_id) to avoid ambiguous-column errors.
Two-letter Indian state code (MH, DL, KA, TN, TS, WB, GJ, RJ, UP, MP, BR, PB, CH, JH, AS, KL, OD). Use for geographic aggregation.
Date the customer registered. Spans roughly the last 2 years relative to CURRENT_DATE. Use for cohort analysis, tenure, and 'new customer' filtering.
One of five values: 'Electronics', 'Apparel', 'Home', 'Books', 'Fitness'. Each category has 20 products. Use for category-level aggregation and filtering.

Current list price in USD. Note: order_items.unit_price captures the historical price paid at the time of purchase, which may differ. Use products.price for current-catalog analysis and order_items.unit_price for historical revenue.

One of five values: 'pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'. For revenue calculations, ALWAYS filter status IN ('paid', 'shipped', 'delivered') — exclude 'pending' (not yet confirmed) and 'cancelled' (revenue reversed). This is the business convention for 'revenue'.

Total order amount in USD, excluding tax. Sum of quantity * unit_price across the order's items. Use for revenue, per-customer spend, average order value. Combine with a status filter for accurate revenue.

Date the order was placed. Spans roughly the last 180 days relative to CURRENT_DATE (seed data is anchored to boot time). Use date_trunc('month' | 'week' | 'day', order_date) for time-series aggregation, and CURRENT_DATE-relative filters for 'this week', 'this month', 'last N days'.
Foreign key to customers.customer_id. Also present in customers table — always qualify (e.g. o.customer_id) in JOINs to avoid ambiguous-column errors.
Foreign key to orders.order_id. Also present in orders table — always qualify (e.g. oi.order_id) in JOINs to avoid ambiguous-column errors.
Foreign key to products.product_id. Also present in products table — always qualify in JOINs.
Number of units of the product in this line item. Always positive. For per-product volume, SUM(quantity) grouped by product_id.

Historical price per unit at the time of purchase (may differ from current products.price). Use quantity * unit_price for accurate historical revenue at the item level; orders.total_amount is the pre-computed order-level total.
Customer full name (first + last). Note: there is no separate email, phone, address, or age column — if the user asks for these, the data isn't available.

Product display name (e.g. 'Wireless Headphones', 'Cotton T-Shirt'). Note: there is no separate SKU, inventory count, weight, or dimensions column — if the user asks for these, the data isn't available.
